official_sources: GOV.UK when permission is required - LDO
Planning Advisory Service Local Development Orders
Plan for Neighbourhoods list of powers
official_measurement_examples: an adopted LDO grants planning permission only for specified development in its defined area
development outside LDO scope can still require a normal planning application
LDO permission does not remove other consent or regulatory regimes
conditions and limitations attached to an LDO remain operative
draft prepared and adopted LDO status must remain distinct
LDOs can be time-limited expired revised or withdrawn
Schedule 1 EIA development cannot be permitted through an LDO and Schedule 2 requires screening controls
Westminster published an adopted Queens Park LDO in May 2026 showing current live LDO use
core_rules: LDO scope must match development and geography
draft LDO is not adopted LDO
expired LDO is not current permission
LDO is planning permission but not other consent
LDO does not override listed-building consent
LDO does not override environmental permits
LDO does not establish access rights
LDO coverage data may be incomplete
historic LGA map is not proof of current status
LDO does not prove infrastructure capacity
no parcel LDO clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
